axiom-bokeh: Glidey fairway driver, a slightly more stable Crave; some runs fly flippy, others stable.
axiom-crave: Straight fairway driver that goes farther than its speed suggests; flight shifts with plastic.
axiom-envy: Throwing putter with surprising distance, but it goes from overstable to flippy as it wears.
axiom-hex: Straight midrange like a Buzzz that feels better in the hand; stability varies by run.
axiom-insanity: Long, fairly understable driver for hyzer flips, but plastics fly very differently.
axiom-proxy: Very straight shallow putter for approaches and short drives; it can flip unless released on hyzer.
axiom-pyro: Overstable midrange that comes out clean forehand; some find it dies quickly with a slower arm.
axiom-tempo: Forgiving low-speed disc thrown forehand for approaches; a few found it too straight.
discraft-zone: Overstable approach disc with a dependable fade, steady in wind; stability changes with beat-in.
innova-destroyer: Overstable distance driver for forehands and headwinds, but stability varies widely between runs.
innova-firebird: Very overstable utility driver for headwinds; it can hook early with less arm speed.
innova-fox: Understable, glidey mid for hyzer flips and wooded lines; it can be too flippy for straight shots.
innova-gorgon: Easy distance from a glidey understable driver; some copies turn over too much or burn out.
innova-leopard: Forgiving fairway driver for newer players; light DX copies can be quite flippy.
innova-mako3: Honest, straight midrange that suits beginners learning form, but it turns over as it beats in.
innova-mamba: Understable distance driver for long hyzer flips and low ceilings; some turn over too easily.
innova-shryke: Longest throws for many, good for open fields and forehand bombs; some copies are too understable.
innova-teebird3: Workhorse fairway driver with a reliable fade; often too overstable for beginners until beaten in.
innova-thunderbird: Neutral to overstable fairway driver with a reliable fade that beats in nicely; it needs some power.
innova-toro: Overstable approach disc thrown forehand, a Zone alternative; it has little glide.
innova-valkyrie: Friendly driver for developing arms with good glide, though it beats in fast and turns over.
innova-wraith: Distance especially on forehand once seasoned; many copies beat in and turn flippy.
kastaplast-berg: Low-glide approach disc that sits where it lands; it gets flippier as it beats in.
kastaplast-jarn: Overstable approach disc best thrown forehand; a few copies were less overstable.
latitude-64-fuse: Straight, glidey understable midrange for tight lines; it gets flippier as it beats in.
latitude-64-pure: Shallow, comfortable putter that holds its line; glide is limited on longer putts.
latitude-64-river: Easy distance and lots of glide for slower arms; it is understable and turns over with power.
mvp-detour: Understable midrange that flips up from hyzer and works through gaps; often flippier than a Hex.
mvp-reactor: Slightly overstable, torque resistant midrange good forehand, which many prefer to a Hex.
mvp-resistor: Very overstable fairway driver, a slower baby Firebird; some copies are extremely beefy.
mvp-servo: Fairway driver seen as a slightly more stable Crave; Neutron and Eclipse come out flippier.
mvp-tesla: More overstable than its numbers suggest and popular forehand; many copies are meathooks backhand.
mvp-trail: Easy distance and glide at modest arm speeds, but copies range from overstable to flippy.
mvp-watt: Straight, floaty throwing putter for upshots that many also putt with; a few report copies warping.
mvp-wave: Distance on hyzer flips at moderate arm speeds, though it often turns over.
prodigy-a2: Very overstable approach disc, often called what a Zone should be; it dumps quickly.
prodigy-a5: Straight to stable approach disc rated for forehands; stability varies by plastic.
streamline-range: Glidey, slightly understable approach disc compared favourably to a Berg; it can turn over.
streamline-trace: Long, straight driver compared to a Wraith, good forehand; some find it too flippy.
westside-harp: Very overstable approach disc, steady in wind; little glide and some plastics turn flippy.
